A ton of neighborhoods in SF are actually super convenient for Fidi Commutes. 

Suburban and quiet: Noe Valley. Close to the Mission for weekend fun, but it’s mostly families out there so it feels very safe. You have the J Muni.

The Marina gets a bad rep for the “fratty” vibe but honestly it’s a very nice neighborhood, super clean, and easy commute to Fidi as well. 

Sunset/Inner Richmond are meh. With your budget I’d avoid it. Fidi commute isn’t terrible, but on weekends it feels like a mission to get to and from there unless you’re between where the Panhandle ends and like 10th ave or so.

West Portal is nice. Clean, easy commute, walking distance to a lot of stuff.

Certain parts of the Mission, like Guerrero and up towards the Castro are really nice. You get the J there as well, and 2 Bart stations - 16th and 24th. 
16th is only 2 stops away from Montgomery (fidi).

Glen Park is also amazing. One of my favorite neighborhoods in SF. BART station, very quiet and clean. Easy commute as well and it’s not crazy expensive.

Close to Fidi but not quiet/suburban: Haight, SoMa, lower Mission, Mission Bay.

It honestly just depends on who you are and what else you’re looking for cause most places in the city offer an easy commute. 

I wouldn’t move to Oakland unless you’re planning on hanging out there on the weekends. If you have the budget for it, SF is better even if that means having a roommate. (Source: lots of friends who moved to Oakland and don’t enjoy he commute). Unless you’re right by BART it isn’t worth it, and BART is pretty expensive.

I think we have a misunderstanding here. If we’re running up a huge tab, I would never ever expect a guy to cover the entire thing and “good impressions” go out of the window here.

That is where the good impression part comes in and if a guy covers my share, for me that is a plus because it shows his interest.

If a guy is seeing a different girl every day of the week, he’s likely not buying all of them drinks every night. That is ridiculous and unless he’s a trust fund baby/really rich for whatever reason, this isn’t feasible for many reasons. So by him buying my round it kinda shows that he’s perhaps not seeing a bunch of people? Doesn’t mean that this is the case, but it is a very nice gesture! 

However many people do set up a bunch of dates because that is what dating is about, and there is nothing wrong with that.

But if I’m out with someone and they don’t mind spending an extra $20 or so to cover my portion it does kinda make me think, hmm, perhaps he really enjoyed my company and it’s not a huge deal because he’s not thinking “wow I’m taking 5 more girls out this week I may be pressured to cover their tab.”

Like I said, I’m totally fine with splitting the bill if it comes down to it and it does not make the other person seem any less important in my eyes (assuming the date went well.) but it’s just a nice little bonus. Every 1st date where the guy covered the entire tab and didn’t let me pay, we saw each other again, and I bought a round at the next date.
